f.title: Produce statistical summaries of drug-event combinations routinely and periodically
f.statement: To limit the chance of failing to detect a signal and to keep processes controlled and predictable in resources, statistical summaries of the information received for each drug-event combination over defined time periods are recommended to be produced in a routine periodic fashion.

rows.quote: To limit the chances of failing to detect a signal and to ensure that the processes in place are controlled and predictable in terms of resources required, it is recommended that these summaries are produced in a routine periodic fashion.

f.title: Define objective criteria for selecting drug-event combinations for further investigation
f.statement: For the same reasons, when possible, the criteria for selecting drug-event combinations (DECs) for further investigation should be objectively defined.

f.title: Alternative signal detection methods may satisfy IR 520/2012
f.statement: The Addendum is guidance on good practice to assist compliance with Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 520/2012 (Articles 19 and 23); other methods may also satisfy this requirement.

f.title: Consider the listed methodological aspects when detecting potential signals
f.statement: The methodological aspects listed in the Addendum should be considered in detecting potential signals; the approach complements classical disproportionality analysis with additional data summaries based on statistical and clinical considerations.

f.title: Monitor the signal detection system for overall and component effectiveness
f.statement: As performance varies between databases, any system of signal detection should be monitored not only for overall effectiveness but also for the effectiveness of its components (e.g. statistical methods and specific group analyses).

rows.actor: Organisation performing signal detection on spontaneous ICSR databases (marketing authorisation holder, competent authority or the Agency)
rows.quote: Thus, a general principle is that any system of signal detection should be monitored not only for overall effectiveness but for the effectiveness of its components (e.g. statistical methods and specific group analyses).

f.title: Pre-specify, validate and fully document the decision to review ICSRs further
f.statement: The decision, based on the assessment of the data summaries, whether more detailed review of ICSRs should be undertaken should so far as possible be formally pre-specified and validated, and in each case it should be fully documented.
f.exceptions: Pre-specification and validation 'so far as possible'

rows.actor: Organisation performing signal detection on spontaneous ICSR databases (marketing authorisation holder, competent authority or the Agency)

f.title: Base the choice of subgroups on empirical assessment of signal detection performance
f.statement: Whether to calculate statistics across the whole database or use subgrouping variables, and which subgroups to use, should be based on empirical assessment of signal detection performance; in particular the impact on the false positive rate should be considered.

rows.actor: Organisation performing signal detection on spontaneous ICSR databases (marketing authorisation holder, competent authority or the Agency)
rows.quote: While the decision is motivated by theoretical consideration, the specific choice of whether to use subgroups and, if so, which to use, should be based on empirical assessment of signal detection performance. In particular the impact on the false positive rate should be considered.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'should' = Recommended.

f.title: Choose the MedDRA level(s) of granularity for automated screening
f.statement: For automated screening of drug-event combinations a choice must be made whether to screen at one MedDRA level of granularity (e.g. SOC, HLT, PT) or several, and whether to include all terms or only a subset; screening at Preferred Term (PT) level has been shown to be a good choice in terms of sensitivity and positive predictive value.
f.clause: IX. Add I.2.1.1. Considerations related to performance of signal detection systems (MedDRA hierarchy)

rows.actor: Organisation performing signal detection on spontaneous ICSR databases (marketing authorisation holder, competent authority or the Agency)
rows.quote: a choice must be made whether to screen at one level of granularity (e.g. SOC, HLT, PT) or several and whether to include all terms or only a subset. f.title: Synonymous MedDRA PTs may be combined for identified areas of interest
f.statement: Some MedDRA terms are effectively synonymous (a primary reporter could not necessarily decide which to use); it may be appropriate to combine such terms when they relate to identified areas of interest.

f.title: Assess signal detection system performance on the database it will be applied to
f.statement: Organisations doing signal detection should assess the performance of a signal detection system directly on the database to which it will be applied, so that the ability to detect new adverse reactions and the workload can be predicted and controlled by appropriate changes to the signal detection algorithm.
f.clause: IX. Add I.2.1.1. Considerations related to performance of signal detection systems (Spontaneous ICSR databases)

rows.actor: Organisation performing signal detection

rows.location: IX. Add I.2.1.1. Considerations related to performance of signal detection systems (Spontaneous ICSR databases)
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: actor named in the source ('organisations doing signal detection').

f.title: Periodically reassess signal detection performance as the database evolves
f.statement: As databases evolve in numbers of ICSRs and mix of medicinal products, periodic reassessment of signal detection performance should be undertaken.
f.clause: IX. Add I.2.1.1. Considerations related to performance of signal detection systems (Spontaneous ICSR databases)

f.title: Apply ongoing quality control when using reporting-frequency change methods
f.statement: Methods for detecting increased ICSR reporting frequency (absolute counts or changes in disproportionality statistics over time) have had limited assessment of effectiveness; they might be implemented with ongoing quality control measures to ensure acceptable performance.

f.title: Create a designated medical events (DME) list as a safety net
f.statement: A list of medical events known on most occasions to result from exposure to medicines, complemented by important and serious events that should not be missed, should be created and can serve as a safety net in signal detection.
f.clause: IX. Add I.3.1. Designated medical events

f.title: Bring DMEs to assessors' attention and prioritise them for clinical review
f.statement: Designated medical events (DME) are recommended to be drawn to the attention of signal detection assessors irrespective of any other statistical methods used, and prioritised for clinical review.

f.title: Apply disproportionality statistics to paediatric ICSRs
f.statement: Statistical disproportionality tools should be applied to ICSRs reported for children to increase the ability to detect signals in the paediatric population from spontaneous ICSR databases.

f.statement: Within-group disproportionality statistics for the paediatric population that are significantly higher than those in the non-paediatric group should be highlighted for additional consideration.

f.title: Use lower ICSR-count thresholds for paediatric signal detection
f.statement: Given the lower number of ICSRs usually received for the paediatric population compared with adults, it is recommended to use lower thresholds based on the number of ICSRs received.

f.title: Use a paediatric targeted medical events list
f.statement: A list of adverse events that tend to have more serious outcomes in children than adults (a targeted medical events list) should be used to reduce missed signals that are more clinically relevant in the paediatric population and otherwise not flagged by other methods.

f.title: Align the paediatric age threshold with GVP P.IV
f.statement: The age threshold for paediatric signal detection should be chosen to align with the upper age limit in GVP P.IV on paediatric pharmacovigilance.

f.title: Geriatric age threshold may be exposure-based or aligned with other PV activities
f.statement: As the age threshold for geriatric signal detection measures is not clearly established, it may be better to choose a threshold based on increased exposure rather than possible increased susceptibility; alternatively, the same age group as selected for other pharmacovigilance activities (GVP P.V) may be used in routine signal detection.

f.statement: For routine signal detection it is recommended that ICSRs from patients above the chosen age threshold are clearly identified and that, as for the paediatric population, within-group disproportionality statistics significantly higher than those within the non-geriatric group are highlighted for additional consideration.

f.title: Display counts of ICSRs coded for abuse, misuse, overdose, medication error or occupational exposure per DEC
f.statement: Because circumstances of use (abuse, misuse, overdose, medication error, occupational exposure) can appreciably alter causality assessment of a potential signal, the numbers of ICSRs with the respective MedDRA codes are recommended to be displayed for each drug-event combination in signal detection listings; between-medicine comparisons of reporting frequency for these codes are unnecessary and potentially misleading.
f.clause: IX. Add I.5. Methods aimed at specific circumstances of medicines use

rows.actor: Organisation performing signal detection on spontaneous ICSR databases (marketing authorisation holder, competent authority or the Agency)
rows.quote:
Hence between-medicine comparisons of reporting frequency of ICSRs with MedDRA-codes describing these circumstances are both unnecessary and potentially misleading.

However, knowledge of these circumstances can appreciably alter the assessment of causality when reviewing a potential signal. Thus, it is recommended that the numbers of ICSRs with the respective MedDRA codes should be displayed for each DEC in signal detection listings.
